context.//: Fleet parameters. Defaults are deliberately small: a sample that cannot be deployed into a new account without a quota increase is a sample nobody runs.
context.//maxTasks: maxTasks x taskCpu must stay within a new account's Fargate vCPU quota, which defaults to 6. 10 x 512 = 5 vCPU, leaving headroom for anything else in the account.
context.//targetBacklogPerTask: Queue items per running task that target tracking holds. Target tracking alone scales out only above the target, so at zero tasks it would never start a batch of this many items or fewer; the scaling function starts an idle fleet itself with ceil(visible / target) tasks, within maxTasks and the pool's concurrency.
context.//creditMargin: Credits held back below each subscription's budget. Passed as CREDIT_MARGIN to both the workers, which refuse a claim at creditBudget - margin, and the scaling function, which counts only subscriptions below that line toward the fleet ceiling. Size it as 2 x C x p95(RunCredits) + 0.01; see the README's Credits section.
context.//egressControl: 'private' = no internet route at all; every destination this workload needs has a VPC endpoint, including the Kiro service via the q endpoint. Costs nothing and is stronger than an allowlist. 'inspection' = NAT plus Network Firewall matching the domains below, for a workflow that needs the internet; ~$288/month standing even at zero tasks. 'open' = NAT and port 443 only, which is not destination control.
context.//kiroEgressDomains: Measured from a capture of a credentialed run, not guessed. Only these two were contacted: runtime carries the model traffic, management the control plane. Telemetry and cognito-identity were also seen and are NOT required — blocking them still produced a successful run. prod.<region>.auth.desktop.kiro.dev was removed after the capture never contacted it: API-key authentication does not use the desktop login flow.
